chunks: From him, from Ja'far, from his father, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I think it is from 'Abdullah ibn Jutha'ah, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a sword adorned with silver, sold on credit (with deferred payment). He said: 'There is no harm in it, because it contains the iron and the silver.'

key_terms.الْحَدِيدَةَ: The iron (referring to the main body)
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a sword with silver inlay be sold on credit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permitted selling a silver-adorned sword on credit, ruling that the silver inlay is integral to the iron blade, thereby constituting a single commodity rather than two distinct items. This ruling is significant in the context of *bay' al-nasi'ah* (credit sales) within Shia jurisprudence, as it clarifies that mixed-material goods do not necessarily trigger prohibitions against exchanging different commodities on credit, provided they are viewed as one unified entity. The hadith highlights the Shia scholarly approach to distinguishing between the essence of an item and its adornment in commercial transactions.
